# Gramlot 0.2.20

- Add `gramlot.format(value, options)` with numeric patterns, positive/negative/zero sections, named date styles, explicit dtype and Intl-based locale/timezone handling. Null produces empty text without applying a mask.
- Carry Page locale and timezone to browser startup. Per-call or per-node options override Page settings; absent Page settings use browser defaults. Live HTML text uses format then mask, retaining typed Data. Masks use `{}` instead of `%s`.
- Add attribute pointer suffixes: `:template` produces text and `:=expression` retains the result type. `{}` supplies the leading value and `{name}` reads another current Source attribute. All attribute inputs are resolved once before use; DOM values are never inputs. Optional `{?}`/`{?name}` admit empty strings, not null. Widget value suffixes are rejected.
- Add expression-local `_F` calling the owning page formatter. Expressions retain existing activation/CSP/lifecycle rules; no global helper or inverse conversion is introduced.
- Port the Italian/English natural-language date-expression parser, including Toolbox corpus alignment. Export `parseDateExpression` with typed result/error declarations.
- Extend documentation with progressive formatting, binding, CSS/Source/DOM and localization/component design records. Component and localization plans do not imply implemented components or translation services.

Verified locally: 3,453 JavaScript tests, 158 Python tests plus 255 subtests; strict Sphinx, mirrored guides and public link checks. Real Chromium and WebKit checks passed single-file and directory serverless exports, typed editing, templates, expressions and page formatting context. Companion gallery tests passed with the progressive c22 lesson.

Limits: advanced number/date patterns and Decimal formatting remain incomplete. Static rendering applies templates/masks but not Intl formatting; expressions remain browser-owned. Python static variable datapath support is unchanged. Optional slots are for pointer templates, not standalone masks. Existing `${name}` behavior remains. Web Components remain a subsequent workstream.
